question: On 1 January 2025, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen presented an altered EU flag. Half of the yellow stars were missing; in their lieu were the colours of the Ukrainian flag. In doing so, Von der Leyen has committed a diplomatic faux pas. No EU treaty protocols allow for this. The design and rules for the use of EU symbols are clearly defined.

The flag’s design was originally defined by the Council of Europe and subsequently taken over by the EC. It is also subject to relevant EU legislation. The design or colours are not allowed to be altered in official contexts. 1.
On what legal basis was the Commission President allowed to present an altered flag?
What could the consequences be if it is not legally justified?
Which Commissioners have criticised the President for presenting an altered flag?
answer: The visual that the Honourable Members refer to is an artistic illustration of the EU and Ukrainian flags, used for communication purposes. It symbolises European solidarity with Ukraine. This is just one of several examples of artistic interpretation of flags used for communication purposes also by other EU institutions. No member of the College has provided comments on the use of this visual.
